title: Proteins — Structure, Classification and Functions
shortDescription: Amino acids, peptide bonds, protein quality scoring and what proteins do in the body and in food.
genZNote: Proteins are the body's builders — and also why dough stretches and egg whites turn solid. Same molecules, different mood.

sections.heading: Chemical Structure
bullets: Building blocks: 20 standard amino acids with amino, carboxyl and variable R groups; joined by peptide bonds.
Primary (sequence), secondary (α-helix, β-sheet), tertiary (3-D folding, disulphide bonds) and quaternary (subunits) structures.
Nine essential amino acids in adults: histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, valine.
Isoelectric point (pI): net charge zero, minimum solubility — casein precipitates at pH 4.6.

table.caption: Protein types
rows: Simple (albumin, globulin, glutelin), conjugated (casein–phosphoprotein, haemoglobin), derived (peptones)
Complete (milk, egg), partially incomplete (wheat — lysine limiting), incomplete (gelatin, zein)

sections.heading: Protein Quality and Food Behaviour
bullets: Measures: PER (rat growth), BV, NPU, chemical/amino acid score, PDCAAS and the newer DIAAS (digestible indispensable amino acid score).
Protein analysis: Kjeldahl nitrogen × 6.25 (milk 6.38; wheat 5.7); Biuret and Lowry colorimetric methods; ninhydrin for free amino acids.
Denaturation (heat, acid, salt, shear) unfolds proteins without breaking peptide bonds — egg white sets, milk curdles.
Functional properties: gelation, emulsification (casein), foaming (egg albumen), water binding (meat), dough formation (gluten: glutenin + gliadin).
Needs: functions include growth/repair, enzymes, hormones, antibodies, transport; 4 kcal/g; ICMR 2020 RDA about 0.8–1.0 g/kg ideal body weight (reference man ~54 g/day, woman ~46 g/day).

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Proteins are polymers of amino acids linked by peptide bonds whose sequence and folding determine function, nutritional quality and food functionality.
keyFacts: Peptide bond joins –COOH of one to –NH2 of next.
Lysine limiting in cereals; methionine in pulses.

highYieldFacts: Cereal + pulse combination gives a balanced amino acid profile.
commonTraps: Denaturation does not break peptide bonds.
Do not call collagen globular — it is fibrous.

questions.prompt: Limiting amino acid in most cereals is:
questions.explanation: Cereals are low in lysine; pulses are low in methionine.

questions.prompt: The nitrogen-to-protein factor commonly used is:
questions.explanation: Kjeldahl N × 6.25 (specific factors for milk and wheat).
